title: C-4 — scheduler_{run_id}.jsonl (Aditya, B)
description:
Three record types, discriminated by `type`.

The `candidates` array is F-3 in full. It is what lets you compute routing-error rate post hoc — for each dispatch, whether an alternative node would have finished materially sooner — and, critically, whether the error came from a BAD POLICY or a STALE ESTIMATE. Without estimate_age_ms per candidate, H3 is unanalysable.

policy.description: F-1: all eight selectable from a single config value, no code change between runs.

staleness_param_s.description: F-8. The s served by the StalenessVeil for this run.

tie_break_draw.description: From the injected rng. Policies hold no state of their own except this.

estimate_age_ms.description: Age of the state estimate this decision was made on, at decide time. Required by H3, which regresses routing error against it. There is no staleness ceiling: a stale node stays selectable, because H3 is about what staleness costs a policy, and a ceiling that hid the stale node would remove the effect being measured.

admissible.description: F-14: applied by the AdmissionFilter OUTSIDE the policy, so every policy inherits it identically.

source.description: `completion_rpc`: a worker's ReportCompletion call on the live scheduler. `sim_completion`: a completion event inside the simulator. `heartbeat`: a completion learned from a heartbeat (no writer today).

observed_lag_ns.description: Residual staleness floor (§2 note 1). Live: the time from the completion RPC reaching the scheduler to the state update it causes, on the scheduler's clock, including any wait for a dispatch holding the state lock. The worker-to-scheduler transit is not in it, because the Completion carries no finish time on a clock both hosts share. Simulator: 0 by construction, since a simulated completion updates state in the same event. The two are not the same kind of number and are not compared.

heartbeat_summary.description: One node's heartbeat sequence as the scheduler saw it (0.2). The first beat from a node sets the baseline, since the worker's emitter outlives each run's scheduler. A node that sent no beat has no record.

missed_beats.description: Sum of (seq - last - 1) over every forward jump in seq.

seq_regressions.description: Beats whose seq was at or below the last one: the worker's emitter restarted.

at.description: When the record was written. The live scheduler has no EndRun of its own and writes at shutdown.
